messages:
jun: heads up — while running long-context stress on MI250X farm I see steady resident growth and a ton of pagewalk stalls in the kvcache path. repro script attached below.

maya: repro script? can you paste the exact command you used? :eyes:

jun: ./tools/run_longctx_kv_repro.sh --model paged-attn --seq 8192 --batch 2 --iters 1500 --gpu mi250x --kv-mode paged
output snippet: 
```
kvcache: alloc page id=0x7fffc0 size=65536 owner=0x14
kvcache: evict page id=0x3fffe age=0x1f refcount=0
PAGEWALK stall @ kernel=pagetable_walk (walks=78214, faults=1489)
GPU stall breakdown: pagewalk 72%, memory-copy 18%, compute 10%
```

samir: that PAGEWALK stall % is wild. does H100 show same?

jun: ran same job on h100-small yesterday: marginal evicts but no steady mem growth. MI250X shows fragmentation + reuse misses after ~200 iters.

linh: could be the sparse-pt->shadowmap remap ordering on ROCm path. we saw similar when PT owner updates weren't atomic across the remap sequence.

maya: can you dump the pagetable metadata (owner epoch, refcount) when we hit thrash? a small trace would help.

jun: pasted short dump at iteration 312: 
```
PT_ENTRY[0x1a3f] = {owner=task-14, epoch=0x7e, flags=0x3} 
PT_ENTRY[0x1a40] = {owner=task-9,  epoch=0x5, flags=0x1}
free_list: head=0x1a55 len=4 fragmented_chunks=[0x1a60,0x1b00,0x1d10]
```

samir: nice. looks like free_list churn + small chunks cause repeated remap and partial page reuse — leads to pagewalks on MI250 because PCIe DMA ordering interacts badly with our async-evict path.

linh: SEP idea: add a lightweight per-page "reuse generation" counter, bump on every remap and compare during lookup to avoid stale owner reads. would require an extra atomic per remap. cheap?

maya: also curious about kernel selection: are we falling back to a non-coalesced pagewalk kernel on MI? that could amplify stalls. jun, any kernel-name logs?

jun: yes kernel printed: pagetable_walk_sparse_rocm_v1 falling back to generic_walk. fallback reasons: misaligned segment and noncontiguous allocations.

samir: can we force coalesced kernel on MI in a debug build and see perf impact? if coalesced reduces pagewalks that points to allocator fragmentation being root cause.

jun: tried forcing it (env REDWOOD_FORCE_PT_COALESCE=1) — fewer kernels but still steady growth, though pagewalk stalls drop from 72% -> 41%. so fragmentation + ordering bug both contributing.

linh: thanks — that supports a two-pronged fix: 1) allocator defragmentation heuristic (merge small chunk allocations when possible) 2) make remap/owner update atomic with CAS and add reuse-gen check in lookup to avoid reading stale owner during concurrent eviction.

maya: can someone open an issue with repro steps, logs, and minimal script? I'll add perf traces and task assignments.

jun: created issue #INF-927 with repro script + logs + H100 vs MI diff (link: https://redwood/issue/INF-927) :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-report: mi250x-farm/slot-12 flagged degraded during run at 2024-10-05T13:02:41Z — auto-evacuation triggered.

samir: assigning: @maya run detailed perf counters (page-faults, TLB-miss, PCIe-stall) on MI250X dedicated node; @jun gather flamegraphs and heap snapshots; @linh prototype atomic remap + reuse-gen check in a branch; I'll coordinate integration testing and cross-gpu repro.

linh: plan for PR: kvcache/pt_remap.cc add atomic owner swap (CAS) + per-page u64 reuse_gen. lookup checks reuse_gen against cached value. add unit test: kvcache/test_repro_pagedrift.cc that spawns concurrent evict/remap + lookup and asserts no stale owner reads.

maya: also add a short telemetry metric: kvcache.page_reuse_mismatch and kvcache.pagetable_fallback_kernel to help detect in prod.

jun: one more oddity — on MI250 we also see occasional NVLINK-like timings despite PCIe; might be ROCm driver doing async copies differently. samir pls check driver versions across fleets.

samir: noted. I will run driver matrix: ROCm 5.7 vs 5.9 and check any kernel ABI fallout. I'll paste matrix in INF-927.

maya: timeline? realistic for a stable patch and telemetry in prod?

linh: prototype + unit test this week, PR early next week, perf runs mid-next-week, telemetry after validation. estimate 2 wks to prod gate.

jun: thanks — tagging here so on-call can watch: @eng-oncall. will post a short alert if we see cluster regressions during tests. :bug:

maya: perfect. if anyone reproduces a different pattern on A100/H100/RTX, drop a short log here. keep replies short so we can triage quickly.

samir: agreed. I'll update INF-927 with progress.

jun: leaving a mini repro gist too: https://redwood/gist/kv-page-drift-repro (includes run_longctx_kv_repro.sh and small flamegraph script)

linh: great. last ask — if you have a capture with perf counters, attach the pcap/trace and I'll run a micro-analysis script to see if ordering anomalies correlate with DMA completion timestamps.

maya: noted. thanks everyone. :party_parrot:
